clue.text: It rouses Albert, getting caught in wrestling hold

parts.note: Al is a short form of the name Albert

indicators.note: in says the letter for caught goes inside the wrestling hold

parts.note: an armlock is a wrestling hold on the opponent's arm
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone called Albert is woken by being trapped in a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A device whose bell or buzzer wakes sleepers is the thing that rouses a person each morning.

clue.text: A prima donna upset, lacking very great opera

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is taken away from what was turned over
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a diva is a prima donna, a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A temperamental leading soprano is upset at missing out on a grand opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns A DIVA into AVIDA; 'lacking' removes V.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Egyptian tragedy is one of the best-loved grand operas.

clue.text: Item once possessed by prodigal son

indicators.note: possessed by means held within, so the answer is held inside the words

explanation.surface: Something the prodigal son of the parable once owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' is an old word meaning likewise, used to introduce each new article in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb item meant likewise or in addition.

clue.text: Democratic principle combining military rank and command

parts.note: a majority is the rank or commission of a major
to rule is to command or govern

explanation.surface: A political principle that brings together army rank and authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority' here is not the larger number but the rank of an army major.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisions taken by the greater number of voters is the basic rule of democracy.

clue.text: Position of tree to be cut

indicators.note: to be cut tells us to cut off the last letter of the tree

parts.note: the locust is a tree, the false acacia or carob

explanation.surface: A tree's location matters because it is about to be felled.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a place or site, the point where something is located.

clue.text: American Indians initially chose great man to attempt rising

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word chose

parts.note: a hero is a great man

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to seek to do something is to attempt it

explanation.surface: Native Americans first selected a great man to try to rise up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SEEK into KEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Part of the world or a kingdom in it? Not quite

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not quite asks for the kingdom's name to be left one letter short at its end

parts.note: Siam was the old name of the kingdom of Thailand

explanation.surface: A geography question asks whether a kingdom lies within some region of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the M of SIAM, leaving SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a continent, the largest division of the globe's land.

clue.text: Closely protect psychiatrist over legal charge, say

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist

indicators.note: say tells us the charge word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in to take the rap

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is guarded tightly over some criminal accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: A rap is US slang for a criminal charge; it sounds like wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink-wrap something is to seal it tightly in clinging plastic film for protection.

clue.text: Take gold to get fine instrument a quick way in Italy

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, a superb instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone uses gold to buy a fine violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An autostrada is an Italian motorway, built for fast travel.

clue.text: Clean garment that's used for work, protectively

parts.note: to dust is to clean by wiping away dirt
a jacket is a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: Someone describes a clean overall worn at the workplace for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a literary work, a book, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper cover wraps a hardback book to protect it, and a book is a work.

clue.text: Animal without tail, by no means sweet

indicators.note: without tail tells us to cut the last letter off the animal word

parts.note: a brute is an animal, a beast

explanation.surface: A beast that has lost its tail turns out to be far from sweet-natured.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut describes the driest champagne or sparkling wine, with almost no sugar.

clue.text: His efforts initially yield negative results

definitions.text: His efforts initially yield negative results

parts.words: His efforts initially yield negative results
parts.note: a film camera user's shots come out first as negatives before prints are made

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a failure, but negative is the film negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking pictures on film gets negatives first, from which prints are made.

clue.text: Involved as thespian or playwright

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters that follow are tangled together

explanation.surface: Someone is taking part either as an actor or as a writer of plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges AS THESPIAN OR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the great comic dramatist of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs and The Birds.

clue.text: In a highly sticky situation?

parts.note: literally, high up in a tree oozing sticky resin; idiomatically, in serious trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means in a fix; 'highly sticky' pictures someone high in a eucalyptus.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a predicament with no easy way out.

clue.text: Eliza or Rose, for example?

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle sells blooms in Shaw's Pygmalion, and Rose is a girl named after a bloom

explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady sells flowers in Covent Garden; Rose is a girl with a flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza sold blooms on the street, and a girl called Rose bears a bloom's name.

clue.text: Formal good manners of a couple of girls, say

indicators.note: say tells us the girls' names are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Polly and Tess are two girls' names

explanation.surface: Two girls are praised for their refined etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, Polly and Tess sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is a French-derived word for formal politeness or courtesy.

clue.text: Peter takes time crossing river as precautionary measure

indicators.note: crossing means having gone across, so time comes after the river

parts.note: peter is old slang for a safe
the Tyne is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone named Peter takes his time getting across a river, as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is criminal slang for a safe, as in a peterman, a safecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a back-up provision protecting against failure.

clue.text: Wrote novel in state prison once

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters of the preceding word are given a new order

explanation.surface: An author produced a book while held in a state jail long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' rearranges WROTE. The Tower of London long served as the state prison for traitors and royal captives.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress by the Thames once held prisoners of the state, such as Anne Boleyn.

clue.text: Energetic type picking up Welsh in this part of Swansea

indicators.note: picking up means taking on board, so one letter is gathered inside the energetic word

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person

explanation.surface: A lively person learns some Welsh while living in a district of Swansea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gower is a peninsula west of Swansea in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the peninsula and district lying within the city and county of Swansea.

clue.text: In port, security man on trawler?

definitions.meaning: a harbour town; this one is in Pembrokeshire, Wales
whimsically, a watchman guarding the catch on a fishing boat

explanation.walkthrough: Fishguard is a ferry port in west Wales; read as two words it is a guard for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour with ferries to Ireland, and a watchman protecting a catch would be a fish guard.

clue.text: Loyal party I'm reforming presents an edifying spectacle

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so the letters of the three words are given a new shape

explanation.surface: A political party's loyal reformers put on a show meant to improve people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforming' rearranges LOYAL PARTY IM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval drama in which virtues and vices appear as characters was staged to teach a moral lesson.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression of quiet Irish writer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken Irish author makes a scornful remark.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of disgust or impatience, like pooh.

clue.text: Safety device that's fitted to bomb.

definitions.meaning: an electrical cut-out wire that melts if the current is too high
the slow-burning cord or detonator attached to an explosive

explanation.definitionFit: A wire that melts to break a circuit protects it, and a timed igniter sets off an explosive.

clue.text: One or more points

parts.note: north, east, south and south again: four compass points by their initials
north, east, south and south again: four compass points by their initials
north, east, south and south again: four compass points by their initials
north, east, south and south again: four compass points by their initials

explanation.surface: A question of whether there is one point or several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means one point, a ness being a headland; 'or' links it to the four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland, a single point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Water supply said to be right

indicators.note: said tells us the word for right is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a reign is the royal right to rule, the period of sovereign power

explanation.surface: Someone says that a supply of water is quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be' links the parts; spoken, reign and rain sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is nature's supply of water to land and reservoirs.

clue.text: Free to be drunk? That's concerning MPs

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds
members of Parliament together make up the House, that is the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether free drinking is a matter for Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is drinks given away by a pub or bar at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink given at the bar's expense costs the customer nothing.

clue.text: Foreign airline making final switch for her

indicators.note: making final switch tells us to swap round the last letters of the airline

parts.note: El Al is the national airline of Israel

explanation.surface: A foreign airline makes one last change of plan on her behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the A of EL AL to the end swaps its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: Person serving passengers dessert was at sea, possibly

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dessert served to passengers was out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges DESSERT WAS; 'possibly' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman cabin attendant looks after travellers on a plane or ship.
